Settlement for escrowed trades

The escrow holds both legs of a trade until each side has signed, then releases them together in one transaction. Nobody can walk away with one leg, and nobody waits for a clearing house to reconcile the books at the end of the day. The contract checks the signatures, the amounts and the deadline, and it refunds both parties when the deadline passes without a second signature. Every step leaves a receipt that anyone can verify on the public ledger afterwards.

  • SPEED — settles in one block
  • COST — one fee for both legs
  • SAFETY — refunds after the deadline
  • PROOF — a receipt per step
  • CUSTODY — nobody holds both legs
  • AUDIT — every signature on chain
  • LIMITS — set per trade
  • KEYS — never leave the wallet
  • FEES — shown before signing
  • ROUTES — one per asset pair
  • ALERTS — sent on each state change
  • EXPORT — trades as a CSV file
  • ACCESS — read-only for auditors
  • STATUS — live on the test network
